title: A finite-variable Tate algebra is an integrally closed domain
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. For $d\ge0$ let $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Then $T$ is a domain, and every element of its fraction field that satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $T$ belongs to $T$. The case $d=0$, when $T=K$, is included.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Proposition 5, printed/PDF p.5 (Tate algebras are unique factorization domains), integrally-closed consequence; read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $D_n=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_n\rangle$. The Gauss norm is a genuine norm by [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] and multiplicative by [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative]. Hence $1\ne0$, and $fg=0$ implies $\|f\|\|g\|=0$, so $f=0$ or $g=0$. Thus every $D_n$ is a domain. We prove by induction on $n$ that it is a normal domain in the explicit sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For $n=0$, coefficient families are just constants, so $D_0=K$ by [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], and its fraction field is itself. This proves the base case.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Theorem 3 and Proposition 5, printed pp.3–5; agent assembly via monic prime factorization over the inductively normal coefficient ring.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and assume $A=D_{n-1}$ is normal. Put $D=D_n$ and $X=U_n$. Grouping coefficients by $X$ gives the isometric ring description in [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion]. For any $0\ne f\in D$, [lem-per-tate-triangular-distinguished-coordinate] gives an isometric $K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$, a unit $v\in A$, and $g=v\sigma(f)=\sum a_iX^i$ with $a_d=1$, lower coefficient norms at most $1$, and upper tail norm less than $1$. Applying [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] gives $g=uw$, where $u\in D^\times$ and $w\in A[X]$ is monic of degree $d$ with all lower coefficient norms at most $1$. Thus $f$ is, up to a unit and an automorphism, such a polynomial. If $d=0$, $w=1$ and $f$ is a unit.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Theorem 3 and Proposition 5, printed pp.3–5; agent assembly via monic prime factorization over the inductively normal coefficient ring.

proof.text: For the monic $w$ just obtained, apply [lem-sfb-normal-domain-monic-prime-factorization] with the inductively normal domain $A$ and its fraction field. It gives $w=\prod_{j=1}^s h_j$ with $h_j\in A[X]$ monic of positive degree and $A[X]/(h_j)$ a nonzero domain. Each $h_j$, and its monic complementary product, has Gauss norm at least $1$, because its leading coefficient is $1$. Multiplicativity [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative] and $\|w\|=1$ force both norms to equal $1$. Hence every coefficient of $h_j$ has norm at most $1$. In particular each $h_j$, regarded as a restricted series, satisfies the division hypotheses with upper tail zero. The empty factor list covers $w=1$.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Theorem 3 and Proposition 5, printed pp.3–5; agent assembly via monic prime factorization over the inductively normal coefficient ring.

proof.text: Fix one $h=h_j$ of degree $e>0$. The inclusion of polynomials induces $\theta:A[X]/(h)\to D/(h)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Division by $h$ in [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] represents every analytic class by a polynomial of degree less than $e$, so $\theta$ is surjective. For injectivity, the basis in [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] represents any polynomial class by $r$ of degree less than $e$. If $\theta([r])=0$, then $r=qh$ in $D$; the two division expressions $r=0h+r=qh+0$ and uniqueness force $r=0$. Thus $\theta$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Theorem 3 and Proposition 5, printed pp.3–5; agent assembly via monic prime factorization over the inductively normal coefficient ring.

proof.text: The quotient $D/(h_j)$ is therefore a nonzero domain, since $A[X]/(h_j)$ is one. Consequently $h_j$ is a prime element of $D$: it is nonzero by its leading coefficient, is not a unit because its quotient is nonzero, and if $h_j\mid ab$, the classes of $a,b$ have product zero in the quotient, so one class is zero and $h_j$ divides that factor. By the quotient map kernel statement [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], being zero in the quotient means exactly membership in $h_jD$. Applying $\sigma^{-1}$ preserves these assertions directly: a product divisible by $\sigma^{-1}(h_j)$ maps to a product divisible by $h_j$. Step 2 and $w=\prod h_j$ now give, for every nonzero $f\in D$, an expression $f=\varepsilon\prod_{j=1}^s p_j$ with $\varepsilon$ a unit and each $p_j$ prime; explicitly $p_j=\sigma^{-1}(h_j)$ and $\varepsilon=\sigma^{-1}(v^{-1}u)$.

source.place: Kedlaya, Tate algebras (2004), Theorem 3 and Proposition 5, printed pp.3–5; agent assembly via monic prime factorization over the inductively normal coefficient ring.

proof.text:
Let $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ satisfy a monic equation $z^m+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}c_i z^i=0$, $c_i\in D$. Its degree satisfies $m\ge1$, since a monic degree-zero polynomial is $1$ and $1
e0$. Choose $z=a/b$, $b
e0$, and use step 5 to write $b=\varepsilon\prod_{j=1}^s p_j$. If $s>0$, put $p=p_1$. Multiplication by $b^m$ gives the explicit identity $a^m+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}c_i a^i b^{m-i}=0$ in $D$, using the injective inclusion into its fraction field. Since $p\mid b$, each summand of the sum is divisible by $p$, so $p\mid a^m$. Repeatedly applying the defining prime-product property shows $p\mid a$: for $m=1$ this is immediate, and for $m>1$ apply it to $a\cdot a^{m-1}$ and descend if necessary. Write $a=pa_1$ and $b=pb_1$, where $b_1=\varepsilon\prod_{j=2}^s p_j
e0$. Cancellation in the fraction field gives $z=a_1/b_1$.

source.place: Tag 0AFV, lemma-UFD-normal, denominator-prime argument written explicitly; prime factorizations here were established in steps 2–5 without invoking a UFD theorem.

proof.text: Iterate step 6 by induction on the finite number $s$ of prime factors of the chosen denominator. The case $s=0$ has unit denominator, so $z=a\varepsilon^{-1}\in D$. The positive case replaces $a/b$ by $a_1/b_1$ representing the same $z$, still satisfying the same monic equation, and with one fewer denominator factor. The induction terminates in a denominator that is a unit, proving $z\in D$. Therefore $D_n$ is normal, completing the dimension induction. Together with step 1 this gives both clauses of the item for every $n\ge0$, with exactly the original completeness and nontrivial nonarchimedean hypotheses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-29a07b1ef (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. The item statement is unchanged, there are no new nodes, and none of the 9 cited nodes depends on the item (closure of 22 nodes checked, so no cycle). The 7 steps are correct. Step 1: Gauss norm from gauss-completion plus multiplicativity gives a domain; base case D_0=K. Step 2: triangular-distinguished-coordinate (r=n>=1) gives a_d=1, lower coefficients <=1, tail <1, which are exactly the hypotheses of weierstrass-norm-division with s=n-1, so g=uw with w monic and ||w||=1. Step 3: normal-domain-monic-prime-factorization over the inductively normal A gives monic h_j with A[X]/(h_j) a nonzero domain; multiplicativity and the monic leading coefficients force coefficients <=1. Step 4: the comparison A[X]/(h)->D/(hD) is surjective by Weierstrass division and injective by the monic basis plus uniqueness of division. Step 5: h_j is prime and so is sigma^-1(h_j); the unit factor is checked. Steps 6-7: written-out denominator-prime cancellation with exponents m-i>=1, induction on the number of prime factors. Hypotheses match: complete field, nontrivial real nonarchimedean absolute value; no discreteness needed. Cases checked: d=0, unit f, w=1, repeated factor, empty factor list. No existing DAG node duplicates the item. Note: the in-unit unsplit lem-trf-tate-separated-monic-quotient (case s=1) already states the step-4 comparison and the report wrongly says none exists; the inline proof is correct and short, so it is kept. Kedlaya Prop 5 is not in literature/ and is marked WANTED; the proof is marked agent-written and does not rely on Kedlaya. Accepted tool_uses: lem-per-tate-triangular-distinguished-coordinate and lem-sfb-normal-domain-monic-prime-factorization. No changes.
